subject: BrightBridge subprocessor notice — onboarding process, objection window, and e-sign path
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Reynolds <mark.reynolds@brightbridge.com>, procurement@brightbridge.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:18:05 -0700
Subject: BrightBridge Subprocessor Notification + DPA redline

Hi Vivek,

Per our contract obligations, please find attached BrightBridge's updated subprocessor list and the DPA redline reflecting the addition of a managed key-store vendor and a new telemetry processor. Documents attached: BrightBridge_Subprocessor_List_v1.xlsx and DPA_Redline_BrightBridge.docx.

Quick summary:
- New processors: KeySafe (KMS provider) and TelemetryOps (metrics ingestion).
- Proposed onboarding flow: 30-day notification with silent acceptance unless Redwood objects in writing within the window.
- DocuSign path: we can send the consolidated DPA for e-sign once we align on objection windows and any targeted redlines.

Can you confirm Redwood's preferred objection process (timing + contacts) so we can prepare the DocuSign envelope? If you foresee technical controls questions, Mark can loop in our security team.

Thanks,
Anita Shah
Contracts Lead | BrightBridge Technologies
Attachments: BrightBridge_Subprocessor_List_v1.xlsx (xlsx), DPA_Redline_BrightBridge.docx (docx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 12:02:18 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBridge Subprocessor Notification + DPA redline

Anita — thanks for the heads up and attachments (received). A couple of quick items from Redwood's side:

1) Objection window: please propose 30 calendar days as the standard notification window, but we will reserve a 15-calendar-day objection window for any processors that handle customer content or key material.
2) Contacts: please list legal@redwood.com and security@redwood.com as the official objection recipients; cc'ing program contacts is fine for context.
3) Signing path: agree that DocuSign is fine. We prefer a single-envelope approach that includes the consolidated DPA and the subprocessor notice as an annex.

Karthik/Laura — looping you both for legal & procurement viewpoint. Karthik, advise on whether our proposed 15-day carve for critical processors needs any additional contractual language (e.g., right to audit, mitigation plan). Laura, FYI for procurement timing — we want to avoid rework during renewal.

Anita — if that fits BrightBridge, send the DocuSign link and we'll circulate to the signatories. Also, please mark the processors in the spreadsheet with an initial "critical" flag if BrightBridge already classifies them as handling customer content or keys.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:33:40 -0700
Subject: Internal: Recommended stance on BrightBridge subprocessor notice

Vivek/Laura — reviewed the DPA redline and subprocessor list. High-level recommendations:

- Accept the 30-day notice as-supplied for non-critical processors.
- For processors flagged as critical (customer content, KMS), we should require a 15-calendar-day objection window and:
  * Right to obtain SOC2 or equivalent attestation for that processor;
  * Minimum contractual commitments around encryption-in-transit and at-rest;
  * Right to require remediation/transition plan (30 days) if the processor cannot meet our controls.
- Suggested redline language: add a short clause to the notice annex: "Customer may object to a proposed subprocessor within 15 calendar days for processors that handle Customer Content or Key Management; upon objection the parties will engage in good faith to remediate or arrange an alternative."

I attached a quick comment summary (Legal_Redline_Comments.pdf) — non-exhaustive. On e-sign: recommend we request a consolidated DocuSign envelope with two signature blocks (BrightBridge exec + Redwood legal & procurement). Requesting a 10-business-day signing window from our side to align internal approvals.

If Laura is good with procurement timing, I'll prepare a short formal response for Anita with the redline text and ask BrightBridge to indicate which processors they consider critical.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Legal_Redline_Comments.pdf
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Reynolds <mark.reynolds@brightbridge.com>, procurement@brightbridge.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightBridge Subprocessor Notification + DPA redline — DocuSign sent

Thanks, Vivek and Karthik — appreciate the quick review and the suggested language. Per Karthik's note, we've added a "critical" flag in the spreadsheet for KeySafe (KMS). TelemetryOps is listed as non-critical.

I've attached the updated annex and created a consolidated DocuSign envelope for the DPA + subprocessor annex. Link below: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345abcde.

Requested timeline from BrightBridge: please review and sign within 7 business days so we can proceed with onboarding KeySafe. We have also attached a short onboarding checklist for KeySafe that includes:
- Evidence of KMS key separation
- SOC2 Type II report or equivalent
- Minimal encryption configuration notes

If Redwood requires any additional attestations or wants to extend the objection window for KMS beyond 15 days, let us know in writing and we can document the exception prior to execution.

Best regards,
Anita Shah
Contracts Lead | BrightBridge Technologies
DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345abcde
Attachments referenced in-envelope: DPA_Redline_BrightBridge.docx, BrightBridge_Subprocessor_List_v1.xlsx
